title: A Hollow for the Veil
premise: Sebastian Villalobos, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-free city of Corvane, discovers that the old gods are answering prayers again—and that her own suppressed power is the beacon drawing them back. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and courted by a resistance that wants to weaponize her, she learns the secret she carries: she is not merely an exile but the last living vessel of the storm god Veyra, whose return would either free the free cities or reignite the god-war that burned the world once before. Torn between loyalty to the found family who sheltered her and the truth that staying hidden dooms them all, Sebastian finally calls the storm—sacrificing her mortal identity to become the veil between gods and mortals, buying the free cities their survival at the cost of ever being human again.
about_author: Beatrix Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal cities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive by becoming someone else.

chapters.title: Salt on the Scales
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In Corvane's night market, she sells harmless luck-charms while concealing real magic beneath suppression tattoos. A desperate mother begs for a true blessing; Sebastian refuses, then secretly heals the woman's child. Emotional beat: the ache of enforced smallness—the first crack in ten years of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Prayer That Answered Back
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The healed child's prayer reaches something ancient, and a voice answers through Sebastian's scars: Veyra stirring. Terrified, she burns her remaining charms. Emotional beat: dread—the past she buried has found her address.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Marrec's POV. The usurper's church detects an anomalous surge in Corvane and opens a hunt for 'the ember.' Marrec, pragmatic and weary, suspects the city itself is lying. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace, with a flicker of doubt in the hunter.

chapters.title: The Gull and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Her found family—the lantern-keeper Odile and smuggler Renn—cover for her during a market raid. Odile reveals she has always known what Sebastian is and kept the secret anyway. Emotional beat: warmth and guilt; loyalty offered without conditions she hasn't earned.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Smuggling a wounded stranger upriver, Renn realizes the man wears the regalia of a drowned temple—and carries a summons addressed to 'the Storm-Caller of Corvane.' Emotional beat: dawning complicity; Renn must choose whether to hand over the letter or his friend.

chapters.title: Nine Names for Rain
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She reads the summons: the old gods' priesthood survives in exile and claims she is Veyra's vessel, the key to restoring them. Flashbacks reveal her exile was engineered—she didn't flee the god-war's aftermath; she caused it. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity collapse.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Concord
chapters.summary: Marrec's POV. Interrogating a captured priest, Marrec learns the usurper's throne rests on a stolen divine covenant—and that the church fears Sebastian more than any army. He begins quietly falsifying reports. Emotional beat: the hunter's crisis of faith.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Silence
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. An old debt comes due: a resistance cell demands Odile deliver Sebastian to them. Odile stalls, buying time but painting a target on the lantern-house. Emotional beat: protective love curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Ember Hunt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marrec corners her in the salt-fog; instead of arresting her, he offers a bargain—her testimony about the stolen covenant in exchange for passage out of the city. Emotional beat: wary alliance between enemies, both lying about how much they trust each other.

chapters.title: Where the Veil Wears Thin
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Guided by the priest's map, she visits a thin place where the gods still listen—and hears thousands of prayers the usurper's church has been devouring to fuel its power. Emotional beat: horror transformed into resolve; the enemy's secret is worse than hers.

chapters.title: The Cellar Beneath the Lantern
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Resistance agents raid the lantern-house seeking Sebastian; Renn fights them off but is captured, and under questioning gives up nothing except a false route. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Marrec's POV. Marrec trades Renn's release for Sebastian's cooperation, betraying his own order's directive. The usurper's armies begin marching on the free cities; the timeline collapses from months to weeks. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into commitment.

chapters.title: Vessel
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The exiled priesthood performs a rite meant to awaken Veyra within her—but Sebastian wrestles control mid-rite, refusing to be erased by the god she carries. She emerges neither fully mortal nor fully divine. Emotional beat: fierce selfhood asserted against destiny.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Garden
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (the usurper, Queen Isolde). Isolde tends a garden grown on devoured prayers and learns of the failed rite. She dispatches her Hollow Knights—not to kill Sebastian, but to cut the god out of her alive. Emotional beat: elegant, patient evil; the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Corvane
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Hollow Knights burn the lantern-house hunting Sebastian. Odile dies holding the door, her last act destroying the ledger of names that would have exposed the resistance. Emotional beat: grief as fuel; the price of survival counted in loved ones.

chapters.title: Everything I Buried
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Consumed by rage, she nearly unleashes Veyra wholesale on the Knights—a storm that would level the city. Renn, freed and broken, talks her down: 'You don't get to avenge us by erasing us.' Emotional beat: the book's thematic crux—grief versus annihilation.

chapters.title: The Covenant Stolen
chapters.summary: Marrec's POV. Marrec delivers proof of Isolde's stolen covenant to the free cities' council, fracturing their paralysis—but the council demands Sebastian surrender herself as a bargaining chip. Emotional beat: political betrayal dressed as diplomacy.

chapters.title: March of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Isolde's armies reach the outer walls; the Hollow Knights breach the harbor wards. Sebastian stands on the seawall between the city and the storm-front she could command. Emotional beat: the point of no return, quiet before catastrophe.

chapters.title: Let It Answer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax. Instead of fighting Veyra for control, Sebastian invites the god in on her terms—carrying the storm rather than being carried by it. She shatters the Hollow Knights and tears the stolen covenant out of Isolde's garden-throne. Emotional beat: transcendence through acceptance, not surrender.

chapters.title: The Price of the Veil
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The covenant restored, the old gods withdraw behind a renewed veil—but a vessel must hold it shut from within. Sebastian realizes the cost: she must leave the mortal world to become the living seal. Emotional beat: devastating clarity; survival for everyone but herself.

chapters.title: What Remains of the Storm-Caller
chapters.summary: Renn and Marrec's alternating POV. Renn releases Sebastian from her promise to stay; Marrec testifies to the council so no one hunts her kind again. Sebastian says her goodbyes at dawn, leaving her suppression tattoos—her mortal name—with Renn. Emotional beat: farewell without bitterness; love outlasting presence.

chapters.title: A Hollow for the Veil
chapters.summary: Epilogue, omniscient-leaning Sebastian POV. Years later, prayers rise again freely, and sometimes rain falls gently on Corvane with no cloud above. Renn keeps a lantern lit in the window; the child from chapter one leaves a charm on the seawall. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—identity surrendered, yet somehow preserved in everything she protected.
